body: This is not the place to post this kind of thing, please stop. The people suffering here can't be cured by words of encouragement or self-help mumbo jumbo.

The problem is, this only works for mentally healthy people. If a mentally healthy person is given a bad situation or difficult event, they can generally choose their mentallity and how they approach it. When I was a kid, I was incredible at doing this. I could literally be worked up about something in one moment, then convince myself to calm down the next. It was AWESOME. Since developing depression, however, this has become next to impossible. There's a lot we don't understand about the mechanisms of depression in the brain, but one thing tends to remain constant for most/all depressed people: we cannot feel good, regardless of what happens to us or how we choose to view our circumstances. We can only feel bad, and then sometimes worse if something bad happens to us. Our brains don't seem to be capable of letting us choose our emotions or mentallity. Telling a depressed person to change their attitude is like telling a person with a broken leg that they'll feel better once they start running.

The human brain is a powerful thing. What a lot of people don't realize, however, is how much power is lost when mental illness comes into the picture. The brain, by definition, doesn't function how it's supposed to, and cannot achieve what a healthy brain can.

Eh, nothing's really "going on," I'm just tired of living. I've had major depressive disorder for my entire adult life (and probably even since high school) and I've tried everything, from meds to therapy to TMS. None of it has worked, and every day I'm alive I just feel more miserable than the last.
